name: Talas
note: De jure capital and largest city, city of governorate significance on the middle Talas River at the foot of the Talas Alatau; c.1,250 m.

name: Nurzhan
note: Oil and refining city (Kobozev 1927–92), city of governorate significance on the lower Chu plain; sits on the site of real Shu.

name: Iyık Janyl
note: Holy city and see of the Syro-Iradi Church on the river flats of the Naryn where it leaves the gorge, ~8 km above Tash-Kömür on State Route 1; most people live on the flats, the old town and cathedral stand on Cathedral Hill above the east bank. Enclosed by Lower Naryn District.

name: Boz-Korgon
note: Fortified government compound (~120 ha), de facto executive seat since 2023; on rising ground beside the road/rail corridor 40 km east of Nurzhan.

name: Köhne Diz
note: Old Talas Citadel Quarter (Old City): Kokand citadel on a terrace above the Talas River; protected zone ~64 ha. Placed just NW of the centre, south of the river.

name: Bazar-i Kalan
note: Covered central market and market quarter on the eastern edge of the Old City (Coppersmiths' Row).

name: Shahr-i Kabud
note: Historic garden quarter north of the Old City on low ground between the old town and the Talas River.

name: Soviet Centre
note: Russian colonial grid town laid out east of the citadel in the 1860s, now the Soviet-era centre with boulevards, central square and mikrorayon estates.

name: Western Corridor
note: Territorial-era western districts toward the air base: Communications Square (Attelkom HQ), Talas Agribusiness Export Zone, Cattle Mart, strip malls; placed ~5 km W of centre.

name: Semiz
note: Mexican-community district (Otkormochny; la Colonia; Meksikanka) ~9 km west of the centre, Trans-Talas Highway on its north edge, SuKarne feedlot to the west; ~25 min by marshrutka.

name: Cottonwood Estates
note: Gated 1997 contractors' estate of wood-frame houses; location unstated, placed in the western corridor between the city and the air base.

name: Alatau Heights
note: Gated foothill suburb (Amerikanka) of 1998–2005 for base contractors and returnees, on the slopes SE of the centre; placed ~4.8 km SE.

name: Northern Industrial District
note: Industrial district on the northern outskirts: Talas Free Economic Trade Zone, Customs Clearance Terminal, municipal cold store.

name: Dastgoh District
note: Historic artisan and foundry quarter (the old quarter) on a branch of the Chu west of the centre; placed ~3.7 km W.

name: Navbahor District
note: Territorial-era residential district of detached brick houses on the southern edge of the city; placed ~3 km S.

name: Central District
note: 1927-plan centre along Azatlık Prospect (ex-Lenin Prospect): House of Soviets, Municipal Library, Palace of Metallurgists.

name: Mikrorayon Estates
note: Numbered five- and nine-storey estates of the 1962 master plan; location unstated, placed NE of the centre.

name: Eastern Industrial Zone
note: Refinery No. 1, bitumen plant, Attelkom Data Center, NAI silos, Zhetysu textile sheds; placed ~4.5 km E of centre.

name: NurGaz Worker Housing Complex
note: Company estate of ~2,800 flats (from 2004) in the northern part of the city; placed ~3 km N.

name: Cathedral Hill
note: Old town on the spur above the east bank of the Naryn around the 1727 Church of St. Janyl, cloister, seminary and pilgrim hostel; reached by the winding Cathedral Hill road over the Naryn bridge.

name: Shahr-i Khunuk
note: Historic summer-house and dacha quarter on a bluff above the river on the upstream (north-east) side of the city, along Khunuk Creek.

name: Lower Town
note: The modern city on the river flats west of the Naryn along State Route 1: Soviet-era blocks, bazaar, orchards and walnut groves toward the hills; home to most of the population.

name: Talas District
note: Talas aimagı, ~9,800 km²: middle Talas valley around the capital incl. the air base, Kara-Bulak and Kara-Oi; seat Talas. Label point east of the city.

name: Kara-Buura District
note: Kara-Buura aimagı, ~11,400 km²: lower/western Talas valley plus a corridor west along the Turksib and Trans-Talas Highway to the Kazakh frontier facing Shymkent (Talas North Terminal); seat Kyzyl-Adyr.

name: Chu District
note: Chüy aimagı, ~24,600 km²: Chu lowlands around Nurzhan, oil fields, canals, Boz-Korgon; borders Kazakhstan east of the city; seat Nurzhan.

name: Sary-Bulak District
note: Sary-Bulak aimagı, ~10,900 km²: southern industrial corridor and foothills south of Talas incl. Sary-Bulak mine, Chatkal smelter and the lower Kara-Suu Canyon; seat Sary-Bulak.

name: Lower Naryn District
note: Tömönkü Naryn aimagı, ~6,300 km²: salient around Tash-Kömür and Iyık Janyl, downstream Naryn cascade, switchyard, Fergana Gateway approach; seat Tash-Kömür.

name: Northern Steppe
note: UN planning zone ~52,000 km²: southern Betpak-Dala north of the Chu and the Moiynkum sands between Chu and Talas; Boztorgoy winter pastures.

name: Karatau
note: UN planning zone ~21,000 km²: Karatau range and foothills running NW toward the Kyzylkum Fringe; Kulan-Talaa plain.

name: Talas Alatau
note: UN planning zone ~17,500 km²: the high range south of the Talas valley, Aksay Plateau, Kara-Koyun, upper Besh-Tash and Kara-Suu, Aksu-Zhabagly, Manas Peak.

name: Chatkal Highlands
note: UN planning zone ~16,000 km²: Chatkal valley and range, Sary-Chelek, walnut forests; Naiman and Sarybagysh pastures.

name: Toktogul–Naryn
note: UN planning zone ~12,500 km²: Toktogul reservoir basin and Naryn gorge down to the dam; Kökjal clan.

name: Fergana Rim
note: UN planning zone ~13,000 km²: rural foothills along the northern and eastern edge of the Fergana Valley (big Uzbek cities excluded); Chubar clan.

name: Kara-Bulak
note: Market town and grain/maize collection point on the valley rail spur, ~35 km west of Talas in the middle valley; Andronovo kurgans; NAI grain depot.

name: Kara-Oi
note: Former Soviet agricultural research station, UNMI headquarters and Joint Liaison Committee venue, on the ISEZ side between Talas and the line, a short way from the Qara-Chik checkpoint.

name: Qara-Chik
note: Foothill village beside the Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint on the road from Talas into the Talas Alatau; gives its name to the ceasefire line.

name: Kalba
note: Village with livestock inspection pens on the road from Talas to the Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint.

name: Ak-Terek
note: Village of white poplars and orchards in the southern foothills of the Talas valley; commuters to Talas.

name: Cholpon-Bulak
note: Horse-breeding and falconry village on the northern side of the valley where the Kyrgyz Range foothills meet the valley floor. (Moved onto the real road in Oct 2026.)

name: Tegirmen
note: Trout-farming village at the confluence of the Urmaral and the Talas, west of the capital.

name: Sarymsakty
note: Garlic and onion smallholdings in the middle Talas valley east of Talas (formed 1994).

name: Kümüshtü
note: Village in the eastern Talas District, upper Talas valley, beside the medieval silver-mining site of Shelji.

name: Kök-Oi
note: Village at the mouth of the Besh-Tash valley ~20 km south of Talas; Besh-Tash Ranger Headquarters and guesthouses.

name: Besh-Tash
note: Village at the mouth of the Besh-Tash valley where the painter Yusup Ayyubov built his house and studio (Ayyubov museum); placed beside Kök-Oi.

name: Sabz-Kand
note: Vineyard village in the foothills east of Talas watered by Kok-Tash kariz galleries.

name: Jangy-Kent
note: Modern village beside the Kara-Khanid mound of Kand-i Nau in the foothills east of Talas, on a kariz branch.

name: Almaluu
note: Apple-orchard and felt-cooperative village in the southern foothills east of the capital.

name: Arsha-Say
note: Village on a side stream of the Talas below the Talas Alatau; birthplace and burial place of the writer Kemel Ishakov.

name: Tash-Bulak
note: Village in the Muz-Suu valley damaged by the 2016 Muz-Köl outburst flood; Muz-Suu placed beside the Urmaral west of the capital (sensors in both valleys).

name: Uuk-Bulak
note: Yurt-frame makers' village in the foothills south-west of Talas.

name: Jangy-Jol
note: 1995 resettlement village for war-displaced families on the southern side of the valley west of the capital.

name: Köpürö-Bazar
note: Village at the road bridge over the Talas west of the capital, near the Central Cattle Mart; wool and hide auctions.

name: Shagyldy
note: Gravel-quarry village on the stony fan of a dry ravine on the northern side of the Talas valley.

name: Teskey-Jar
note: Village on a loess terrace above the gorge of the upper Talas, eastern Talas District (2004 cliff collapse).

name: Toguz-Bulak
note: Roadside village and snowplough depot at the foot of the southern approach to the Kök-Bel Pass (Talas–Chu road).

name: Kyzyl-Adyr
note: Administrative centre of Kara-Buura District on the Trans-Talas Highway, lower Talas valley; horse fair; Kyzyl-Adyr Reservoir nearby.

name: Bakyyan
note: At chabysh horse-training village ~8 km east of Kyzyl-Adyr in the lower Talas valley.

name: Ak-Tash
note: Limestone-quarry village in the western foothills of the Talas Alatau above the lower valley; State Defense Corps Ak-Tash Training Center; kariz-watered fields.

name: Taldy-Suu
note: Willow and honey village on a side channel of the Talas River in the lower valley.

name: Ak-Döbö
note: Village partly on a Bronze Age/medieval settlement mound in the lower Talas valley.

name: Ming-Örük
note: Orchard village on the Kenkol fan where the river leaves the Talas Alatau for the western valley, near Karool-Döbö and the Kenkol burial ground; kept west of Kara-Bulak so it stays in Kara-Buura.

name: Eski-Korgon
note: Village around an 1830s Kokand fort on the old road down the lower Talas valley toward the Kazakh border.

name: Chet-Bulak
note: 1908 Russian settlers' village with a single poplar-lined street on the northern side of the lower Talas valley.

name: Sary-Bulak
note: Antimony mining village (workers' settlement 'Rudnik') and district seat in the Talas Alatau foothills ~28 km south of Talas; reached by a branch road from the Kara-Suu canyon mouth. Placed SSW so the Besh-Tash valley (Talas District) stays separate.

name: Chatkal
note: Works settlement of ~6,000 beside the Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex in the Talas Alatau foothills ~30 km south-west of Talas (named after the Chatkal range, outside its basin).

name: Ak-Bulak
note: Beekeeping and trout-pond village in the Sary-Bulak District foothills south of Talas; some residents work at the mines and Chatkal smelter.

name: Tunuk-Bulak
note: Karst-spring village in the limestone foothills south of Talas (same belt as the Kyrk-Kazyk Caves and Maryam-Bulak).

name: Besh-Terek
note: Sugar-factory village (Chui Sugar Refining Corp.) in the irrigated lowlands west of Nurzhan.

name: Shahr-i Nav
note: Grid-plan 1960s state-farm village on the Jangy-Aryk branch canal north of Nurzhan.

name: Besh-Moinok
note: Melon village at the tail of a branch canal on the northern edge of the irrigated land NW of Nurzhan, where farmland meets the Moiynkum sands.

name: Jon-Aryk
note: Koryo-saram rice village founded 1937–38 on the lower Chu south-west of Nurzhan.

name: Shaar-Döbö
note: Village ~30 km west of Nurzhan beside the Sogdian/Kara-Khanid site of Shahr-i Buzurg.

name: Kum-Aryk
note: Greenhouse village on the eastern outskirts of Nurzhan near the oil fields (gas flaring).

name: Sary-Döbö
note: Village (ex-Zheltaya Mogila, 1891) around the ruined fort of Diz-i Zard in the lower Chu valley; placed downstream (NW) of Nurzhan. (Moved onto the real road in Oct 2026.)

name: Temirchi
note: Blacksmiths' village ~15 km north of Nurzhan.

name: Kök-Döbö
note: Village on a low hill on the southern side of the Chu lowlands SE of Nurzhan; weather radar on the summit.

name: Aral
note: Village on a strip of land between two channels of the Chu west of Nurzhan.

name: Uch-Emchek
note: Sugar-beet village beside three hillocks west of Nurzhan, supplying the Besh-Terek factory.

name: Tash-Kömür
note: Coal-mining town on the Naryn at ~600 m where it leaves the mountains; seat of Lower Naryn District, UNMI sector HQ, south end of State Route 1 (236 km from Talas).

name: Kapka-Tash
note: Village below Tash-Kömür on the road toward the Uzbek border at the mouth of a short side gorge of the Naryn.

name: Jyluu-Bulak
note: Spa village with 42 °C sulfur springs in a side valley of the Naryn above Tash-Kömür.

name: Bulak-Bashy
note: 1965 dam-builders' village on the Naryn above Tash-Kömür; hydropower and switchyard workers.

name: Altyn-Bulak
note: Mineral-water bottling village in the foothills north of Tash-Kömür.

name: Kara-Suu
note: Tanıp clan centre in the upper Kara-Suu valley above the canyon: Kara-Suu Tribal Elders Council Hall, rural health centre, winter houses; the lore names the valley, not a village (label point).

name: Chong-Kapka
note: Chongtor-breeding winter village on Tanıp pastures in the upper Kara-Suu valley, just above the rock gateway where the river leaves its upper valley (head of the Kara-Suu Canyon).

name: Upper Besh-Tash
note: Akjele clan homeland in the upper Besh-Tash valley on the tribal side of the line (no village name given; label point).

name: Kara-Koyun
note: Karakoyun clan winter gathering place in the Kara-Koyun Valley south of Kara-Buura District near the line; stone pens and winter houses; extraordinary Kurultai venue.

name: Kashka-Jol
note: Pack-horse hamlet in the middle Kara-Buura valley on the old route over the Kara-Buura Pass to the Chatkal.

name: Kyrk-Bulak
note: Spring-line village in the limestone foothills of the western Talas Alatau, south of Kara-Buura District; Chongtor breeders.

name: Kyrk-Choro
note: Village in a valley below the northern face of Manas Peak at the western end of the range; manaschy gathering each August.

name: Orto-Ayyl
note: Upper Talas valley village just beyond the Qara-Chik line; council of elders under adat since 2008.

name: Kara-Kungey
note: Apple and potato village on the sunny side of a valley in the northern Talas Alatau.

name: Otmek
note: Staffed weather station and hamlet (~20 people) below the Otmek Pass (3,330 m) on the old road from the Talas valley into the Suusamyr.

name: Karakol-Ashuu
note: Seasonal camp (stone hut and stables, two or three families in summer) at the foot of the northern ascent to the 3,450 m Karakol pass.

name: Karakol
note: High village at ~2,300 m in the upper Western Karakol valley on the eastern Talas Alatau near the Suusamyr; end of the all-weather road; logistics depot.

name: Ak-Kyya
note: Summer settlement of ~70 herding families in the Irad part of the Suusamyr valley; regional ulak tartysh tournament.

name: Kosh-Döbö
note: Seasonal herders' camps (~400 people, June–September) around a low hill on the Aksay Plateau near the Kurultai grounds.

name: Kanysh-Kiya
note: Largest village of the Chatkal valley: secondary school, hospital, weekly market, gold washing (approximate real location). (Moved onto the real river in Oct 2026.)

name: Terek-Sai
note: Former Soviet gold/antimony mining village; Isyk-Bulak warm springs nearby (approximate real location).

name: Arkyt
note: Village at the southern entrance of the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve; reserve headquarters and warden service.

name: Kök-Jar
note: Former antimony exploration mining village in the upper Chatkal valley below the Kök-Jar Pass; four-classroom school; snow-leopard wardens.

name: Kyzyl-Bel
note: Sheep and yak hamlet in the upper Chatkal valley at the foot of the Kyzyl-Bel Pass (2,450 m).

name: Teke-Tash
note: Village at ~2,250 m on the southern slopes of the Talas Alatau above the Chatkal valley, at the upper limit of spruce.

name: Archaly
note: Village in a forested side valley of the Chatkal (spruce and juniper).

name: Bel-Aldy
note: Pack-guide hamlet at the foot of the bridle paths over the Chatkal range to the northern Fergana Valley.

name: Muz-Tör
note: Guides' hamlet below the glaciated crest of the Chatkal range beside a 1972 Soviet mountaineering camp.

name: Jashyl-Köl
note: Summer yurt settlement of ~25 families on a moraine lake at ~2,600 m on the southern slopes of the Chatkal range, on the route to Sary-Chelek.

name: Besh-Köl
note: Summer herders' camp (8–10 families) at ~3,000 m beside five glacial lakes in the upper Chatkal range.

name: Toktogul
note: Market town on the northern shore of the Toktogul Reservoir (Ketmen-Töbö basin), rebuilt in the 1970s; ISEZ since the 2009 corridor protocol.

name: Kara-Köl
note: Town built for the Toktogul dam's construction workers and operators a short distance below the dam; in the ISEZ since the 2009 corridor protocol.

name: Ozgörüsh
note: 1974–75 resettlement village on the lower Uzun-Akmat above the reservoir; Uzun-Akmat Terraces; Kökjal clan elder's home (approximate location).

name: Jele-Döbö
note: Trout-cage and orchard village on the northern shore of the Toktogul Reservoir.

name: Kara-Jylga
note: Remote village at the head of a side valley north of the reservoir, 24 km dirt track (cut off by avalanches 2012, 2026).

name: Tash-Köröö
note: Cobble-built goat-herding village in a side valley above the reservoir, below a box canyon used as a pen.

name: Kara-Say
note: Barley-terrace village at ~1,900 m in the Fergana Range foothills above the Toktogul basin.

name: Kosh-Bel
note: Hamlet (~150 people) at ~2,400 m on the migration route from the Toktogul basin to the Fergana Range pastures; veterinary post.

name: Dary-Bulak
note: Summer yurt encampment (~30 families) around warm and cold springs on the high pastures of the Fergana Range.

name: Bazar-Korgon
note: Market town at ~800 m on the Kara-Unkur near the Uzbek border; walnut bazaar, Sunday livestock market; Chubar clan centre and Muslim centre.

name: Arslanbob
note: Walnut-forest village at ~1,600 m in the upper Kara-Unkur valley ~40 km NE of Bazar-Korgon; Arslanbob-Ata shrine, waterfalls, guesthouses.

name: Mailuu-Suu
note: Former Soviet uranium town at ~1,000 m on the Mailuu-Suu River, ~20 km east of Tash-Kömür, beside the line around Lower Naryn; tailings.

name: Kyzyl-Unkur
note: Village in the Kara-Unkur valley named in the Oct 2026 tremor report (epicentre a few km NE); a real village of this name exists, but it is placed here between Bazar-Korgon and Arslanbob to match the report.

name: Sopol-Tepa
note: Uzbek-speaking potters' village near Bazar-Korgon by the Chopo-Jar clay bluffs.

name: Korgoncho
note: Uzbek-speaking village of walled Kokand-era farmsteads on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley.

name: Örüktü
note: Terraced apricot village on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley.

name: Boz-Adyr
note: Rain-fed wheat village in the loess adyr foothills of the northern Fergana Valley, kept well north of Namangan.

name: Kara-Jygach
note: Walnut-harvest village at the lower edge of the walnut-fruit forest on the southern slopes of the Chatkal range above the Fergana Valley.

name: Jangak-Bulak
note: Village inside the walnut-fruit forest on the southern slopes of the Fergana Range west of Arslanbob; sacred walnut grove.

name: Bazar-Terek
note: Thursday wool and sheep market in the Karatau foothills where tracks from the Kyzylkum Fringe winter pastures meet the road to the Talas valley.

name: Hauzdy
note: Hamlet beside the ruined caravanserai of Rabat-i Kamal on the old road along the Karatau foothills west of the Talas valley.

name: Tar-Say
note: Red-clay hamlet at the mouth of a Kök-Moinok canyon in the Karatau foothills (2016 flash flood).

name: Kyzyl-Döbö
note: Saddlers' village at the foot of red sandstone cliffs in the Karatau foothills; sells at Bazar-Terek.

name: Bitik-Tash
note: Petroglyph village in the Karatau foothills.

name: Kök-Say
note: Village in a limestone gorge of the Karatau reached by a single dirt road.

name: Tuzduu
note: Brackish-well camel and sheep village on the edge of the Kulan-Talaa plain in western Irad.

name: Sasyk-Bulak
note: Village at the foot of the Karakyr Range on the western edge of Irad; raptor-count base.

name: Ak-Jar
note: Karakul-sheep village under a limestone escarpment near the Kazakh border on the semi-desert western edge.

name: Tört-Kuduk
note: 1964 hydrogeological-expedition village on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala; supply point for the Keng-Talaa pastures.

name: Ak-Jal
note: Horse-herding village on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala near the Keng-Talaa race course.

name: Kaiyrma
note: Reed-cutting and fishing village on the lower Chu below the irrigated zone. (Moved onto the real river in Oct 2026.)

name: Kamyshtuu
note: Reed and muskrat hamlet beside drainage marshes on the northern edge of the irrigated Chu lowlands, at the edge of the sands.

name: Tash-Kuduk
note: Hamlet at a 15th-century stone-lined well on the old track across the southern Moiynkum sands.

name: Ak-Chiy
note: Chiy-screen weaving village on the salt flats of the southern margin of the Moiynkum sands.

name: Zhalgyz-Terek
note: Hamlet at a poplar-shaded spring on a track across the Moiynkum sands.

name: Töö-Kuduk
note: Camel-herding hamlet at a well in the western Moiynkum sands.
